small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs targeting 4090 (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=4 stages=5, and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32) since M=N=K=8192 is square and the current configs may be picking suboptimal large tiles; also try GROUP_M=16 to improve L2 reuse for the wide N=8192.
- Cast bias once to fp16 and load as fp16 to avoid the extra fp32 load + upcast in the epilogue; keep accumulator fp32 but materialize bias add in fp16 vector.
- Output directly to fp16 (already done) but skip the `.to(torch.float16)` of x at every forward call by caching nothing — instead, fuse the fp32→fp16 cast of x into the kernel's A-load (load fp32, cast in-register) so the user-visible input copy disappears.
large_guidance:
- Consider a split-K or persistent-GEMM design: with M=N=K=8192 and only 64×64=4096 tiles at 128×128, a persistent kernel with one program per SM iterating over output tiles can amortize launch/scheduling and improve L2 reuse versus the current one-program-per-tile launch.
- Avoid the fp32→fp16 input materialization entirely by writing a kernel that consumes fp32 x and fp16 wT directly (mixed-precision tl.dot via cast-on-load), eliminating an 8192×8192×4B intermediate allocation+write each forward.
- Explore using tensor-core-friendly bf16 weights instead of fp16 if numerical headroom allows; on Ada, bf16 tl.dot has the same throughput and slightly better tolerance, letting you skip the fp32 bias upcast path.
